subject.title: [Bug]: Chrome extension browser relay removed with no cross-machine  replacement (regression)

question: Should OpenClaw restore a Chrome-extension remote browser relay, replace it with a browser-backend/plugin API or node-host bridge, or intentionally keep the legacy relay retired?
rationale: The requested behavior crosses browser-control security, signed-in-session access, remote Gateway operation, extension packaging, public config/API, and plugin ownership decisions that automation cannot safely choose by widening the driver enum.

options.title: Design a vetted replacement
options.body: Define the safe browser-control contract first, then land an extension bridge or browser-backend seam with auth, scoping, migration, docs, and live cross-machine proof.

options.title: Wait for My Browser path
options.body: Let the node-anchored My Browser PR stack settle, then evaluate whether it satisfies the managed-hosting cross-machine relay requirements or needs follow-up work.

options.title: Keep relay retired
options.body: Make an explicit maintainer decision that the legacy relay will not return, then close the cluster with clear docs for node host, remote CDP, and external project alternatives.

recommendation.title: Design a vetted replacement
recommendation.body: Define the safe browser-control contract first, then land an extension bridge or browser-backend seam with auth, scoping, migration, docs, and live cross-machine proof.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc owns the strongest direct history for the relay removal and MCP migration that created the current behavior.
